records.name: Codex Sinaiticus
records.date_estimate: Generally dated to the 4th century; a published reassessment argues a possible range from early 4th to early 5th century
records.contents: Extensive portions of Greek Hebrew Scriptures and Apostolic Writings. The Codex Sinaiticus Project identifies the Sirach section from the grandson's Prologue at quire 68, folio 1 recto through quire 71, folio 2 recto; individual verse coverage and lacunae require extraction from the TEI transcription.
records.holding_institution: British Library; Leipzig University Library; National Library of Russia; Saint Catherine's Monastery
records.status: metadata catalogued; pinned electronic transcription importer and offline page reader integrated into the Android build; manuscript images remain external
records.caution: Do not present the middle of the 4th century as an exact date; portions are held by multiple institutions. The repository transcription is imported during the Android APK build under its separate CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 licence.

records.name: Codex Vaticanus (Vat.gr.1209)
records.date_estimate: 4th century CE according to the Vatican Library catalogue
records.contents: Surviving original manuscript: Matthew–2 Thessalonians; Hebrews 1:1–9:14; James–Jude. The manuscript does not preserve the Pastoral Letters, Philemon, or Revelation. The Revelation now bound with the codex is a later fifteenth-century supplement and is not part of the original codex.
records.condition: Incomplete parchment codex; original New Testament leaves survive for the stated range. The ending of Hebrews is lost after 9:14; later supplements must be distinguished from the original manuscript.
records.status: metadata catalogued; INTF NTVMR transcription imported at APK build time as offline page-indexed source records
records.caution: Do not claim that the original Codex Vaticanus contains the Pastorals, Philemon, or Revelation. The later Revelation supplement is a separate manuscript. Preserve the codex's missing leaves as physical losses, not as textual omissions. Do not fill its readings from another edition.
